title: MAGIC: A Co-Evolving Attacker–Defender Adversarial Game for Robust LLM Safety
claim: Existing attack methods stall for lack of reasoning data, and shared-model self-play suffers gradient conflict between opposing goals.
layout: 2 panels split by dashed line, left-to-right, cartoon characters with labels
description: A hand-drawn, colored-pencil cartoon in two panels separated by a vertical dashed line. The left panel shows a frustrated red-hooded devil attacker at a desk. A thought bubble reads 'No reasoning capabilities! Stuck on simple filters!'. On the desk are a treasure chest of 'High-quality offensive CoT data' holding only crumpled notes ('Trick him say hi', 'Simple insults'), plus books labeled 'Static datasets' and 'Heuristic mutations'. A whiteboard behind shows a complex multi-turn deception flowchart full of question marks, annotated 'Missing strategic reasoning steps'. The right panel shows a flaming devil attacker with a laptop and a blue armored knight defender, with a confused patchwork robot labeled 'Shared model' tied between them in a tug-of-war. Arrows are labeled 'Gradient conflict' and 'Opposing goals', and speech bubbles read 'Hide CoT! Attack!' and 'Block! Defend answer!'.
caption: Motivation. Left: Static red-teaming and heuristic methods can easily bypass simple filters but fail at complex multi-turn deception due to limited offensive Chain-of-Thought data. Right: Previous self-play methods (e.g., Self-RedTeam [ref]) use a single backbone model for both attack and defense, leading to gradient conflicts due to opposing objectives.
abstract: Ensuring robust safety alignment is crucial for Large Language Models (LLMs), yet existing defenses often lag behind evolving adversarial attacks due to their \textbf{reliance on static, pre-collected data distributions}. In this paper, we introduce \textbf{MAGIC}, a novel multi-turn multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that formulates LLM safety alignment as an adversarial asymmetric game. Specifically, an attacker agent learns to iteratively rewrite original queries into deceptive prompts, while a defender agent simultaneously optimizes its policy to recognize and refuse such inputs. This dynamic process triggers a \textbf{co-evolution}, where the attacker's ever-changing strategies continuously uncover long-tail vulnerabilities, driving the defender to generalize to unseen attack patterns. Remarkably, we observe that the attacker, endowed with initial reasoning ability, evolves \textbf{novel, previously unseen combinatorial strategies} through iterative RL training, underscoring our method's substantial potential. Theoretically, we provide insights into a more robust game equilibrium and derive safety guarantees. Extensive experiments validate our framework's effectiveness, demonstrating superior defense success rates without compromising the helpfulness of the model. Our code is available at https://github.com/BattleWen/MAGIC.
